scenes.narration: A child often needs to behave a little differently from its parent. Today we change methods, or extend them.

scenes.onScreen: "Change or extend": three numbered lines (1. Same method name in the child replaces the parent's; 2. super().method() runs the parent's version; 3. Python looks in the child first) and an analogy card: a family song: the child sings the same tune but changes a verse, or sings the old verse and adds a new one
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: If a child class defines a method with the same name as its parent, the child's version wins. This is called overriding. Python looks in the child first, then in the parent. Sometimes you want both. Call super dot method inside the child's version, to run the parent's code first, and then add more. Think of a family song. The child sings the same tune, but changes a verse, or sings the old verse and adds a new one.

scenes.narration: Here is how Python finds a method. It looks in the object's own class first. If the method is there, it runs. If not, Python walks up to the parent, and checks there. The first match wins. So the child can override the parent, and objects with no override use the parent's version.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: calling the parent wrongly
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We call the parent's init through the class name, and pass only the name. Python needs self as the first argument, and it does not add it here. Our name is taken as self, and the real name is missing. Type error, init missing one required positional argument, name. Use super dot init instead. It passes self for you.

props.error:
File "parent.py", line 7, in __init__
    Animal.__init__(name)
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^
TypeError: Animal.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'name'

lines: TypeError: Animal.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'name'

props.why: Calling a method through the class name does not pass self for you. Calling it through super() does, so super() is the safe way.

scenes.onScreen: Why did the method override its parent? It needed some independence.

shorts.hook: "Overriding means a child defines a method with the same name as the parent's."
shorts.script: Overriding means a child defines a method with the same name as the parent's. The child's version wins. A dog's speak returns Woof, while a plain animal's speak returns dots. Same name, different behaviour. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: The child's version wins.

shorts.title: Python lookup
shorts.script: How does Python find a method? It looks in the object's own class first. If it is not there, it goes up to the parent, and keeps going up. The first match wins. A fish with no speak of its own simply uses the parent's. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Python looks up the tree.

shorts.title: Extend with super
shorts.hook: "You do not have to throw away the parent's method."
shorts.script: You do not have to throw away the parent's method. Call super dot speak inside the child's version, to get the parent's answer. Then add your own part. Extending beats copying, because a fix in the parent reaches every child. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Extend, do not copy.

shorts.title: The wrong call
shorts.script: A frequent mistake. You call Animal dot init with just the name. Python says, type error, init missing one required positional argument, name. Through the class name, self is not passed. Use super dot init, and Python passes self for you. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Use super().
